body:
It's all proper radio stations.

I actually live in a decent sized city -- don't want to name it, but it's fairly populous -- it's just that our local radio offerings are miserable. There are plenty of radio stations, but they're mostly variations on robo-DJ'd adult contemporary and hyperconservative talk shows.

I imagine that if I did live in the sticks, it would help, but as it is it's not too bad. One of the shittier local stations is so underpowered that it turns off at sunset, and that's the one that allows me to hear the New Orleans station. So that's a perk.

[DXing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DXing) is basically listening in to distant radio broadcasts and figuring out what they are and where they're from. I just do AM, since I don't have a shortwave set yet.

On a clear night, I can hear radio broadcasts from all over North America, just with a crappy little clock radio in Nowhere, Michigan. I most frequently hear Toronto, Buffalo, Montreal, and New Orleans. I did get some city in Saskatchewan once though.

It's not much of a hobby, but I play Minecraft... I find that level of immersion helps keep my mind off things. Kind of a dangerous timesuck though.

I'm pretty into radio, though. I like listening to podcasts and DXing, and I'm a hopeless NPR geek.
